cannot_decide: Which path is right: no ground truth for arm amplitude exists here, so this cannot say whether two-view shrinks motion or monocular inflates it, and hold-x's motivation depends on that. Whether YouTube's remainder is signers, clip cutting (0.57 s per token, against D20's 0.30) or framing. Whether a stored 24 fps is the sources' true rate: the clock check moves with signers too. A channel is not a signer. ASLLRP's path was not compared on the same clips. Carry: the word is defined nowhere in the repository, so 1.44x is neither confirmed nor refuted: on hold-x it needs the right wrist at the row's right_needed_for_1_44.
note: Real signing's wrist differs by signer and by corpus far more than the review's first numbers show one by one. Same clips through both paths: pooled, the monocular path reads 18-39% more wrist motion at 3 Hz and 23-37% more spread than two-view on every How2Sign signer, while its raw speed is 0.83-1.11x. Per side it is not every signer: at 3 Hz the left is 1.36-1.65x and the right 0.94-1.23x (c03's right is below 1), and raw the right is 0.73-0.98x. Either direction fits: two-view could shrink the motion, or the monocular path could inflate it, and monocular inflation fits the left-arm asymmetry at least as well as two-view shrinkage. Median clip seconds differ 1.00-1.05x between the paths, so frames are not exactly paired. Content above 3 Hz is not called jitter here: nothing shows how much of it is tracker noise. Both How2Sign paths store 24 fps. With the path matched, YouTube still reads about 1.5x D20 raw and at 3 Hz. The word clips' training is mostly monocular (word_clip_path: 0.27% of one-word weight, 8.8% of sampling and 27.2% of sentence-token weight are two-view), so composition against D20 through the same path may be the like-for-like comparison (composition_on_monocular): top10 1.88x raw and 1.75x at 3 Hz, against 1.77x and 2.20x on two-view. That is an inference: the decoder's share is not measured and no generated clip's amplitude was tested. YouTube's channel ranges rest on 5 clips each. YouTube's corpus row and that range also dropped channels with no number at all (youtube.hole_check). The plan records the span on main; no claim, gate or rule reads it until an independent review of this rerun.

real_signer_span.definition: p10 and p90 of per-signer mean wrist speed, signers or channels with at least 30 clips holding a number on every rate and side, all through the monocular path; real clips only; never c00 or a test partition
real_signer_span.note: c01, c03 and c05 are D20's clips through the monocular path. A channel is not a signer. A channel's clips are those of its videos with a tracked body, so a channel's number leaves out its untracked clips (reports/youtube_wrist_validity.json). Set after composition's figures were known, as the plan's section says.
real_signer_span.reads_it: no claim, gate or rule, until an independent review of this rerun

reference.note: D20 metadata and motion are the reference only; nothing is fitted on them

word_clip_path.answer: mostly monocular in training: two-view is 0.27% of the weight teaching a cached word alone (How2Sign's weight 78 of 29344), 8.8% of sampling and 27.2% of the sentence-token weight. The decoder's share is not measured: the tokenizer weights How2Sign x2 and its layout is the conform target. No generated clip's amplitude was tested, so reading composition against D20 through the monocular path as like-for-like is an inference.
word_clip_path.note: New entries' sources are ASLLRP segments or isolated clips of the same mix, both monocular. A corpus's path is read from its state prefix and the script that built it; no state was re-extracted to confirm it.

semlex-text-v2.path: monocular (scripts/extract_semlex_videos.py: 'exactly the extraction and solver of our other corpora')
